body:
We wanted to provide an update on the status of the Character’s Chapter 11 case.

On November 4, 2026, the Bankruptcy Court entered an order approving bidding procedures to govern Character’s sale process (the “Bidding Procedures Order”). The Bidding Procedures Order also approved a form of notice (the “Transaction Notice”) containing important information related to the Company’s ongoing sale process. A copy of the Transaction Notice is reproduced below.

For more information relating to the Chapter 11 case, or to obtain copies of motions, orders, including the Bidding Procedures Order, and other documents discussed in the Transaction Notice online, you can visit the website administered by the Company’s claims and noticing agent, Stretto, Inc.: https://cases.stretto.com/chartech/ .

NOTICE OF PROPOSED SALE OF ASSETS, STALKING HORSE TRANSACTION AGREEMENT, BIDDING PROCEDURES, AUCTION, AND SALE HEARING

PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that the above-captioned debtor and debtor-in-possession (the “ Debtor ”) filed a voluntary petition for relief under chapter 11 of title 11 of the United States Code, as amended (the “ Bankruptcy Code ”), on October 12, 2026, in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware (the “ Bankruptcy Court ”). The Debtor is seeking to sell, license or dispose of (the “ Sale ”) all or substantially all of its assets (the “ Assets ”) free and clear of all liens, claims, interests, and encumbrances to the fullest extent authorized by section 363 of the Bankruptcy Code.

PLEASE TAKE FURTHER NOTICE that in connection with the Sale, the Court has approved the Debtor’s designation as a stalking horse agreement, the Stalking Horse Transaction Agreement, dated as of October 13, 2026 (the “ Stalking Horse Transaction Agreement ”) for the sale or license of certain assets (the “ Disney Target Assets ”) with Disney Worldwide Services, Inc. (“ Disney ”), free and clear of all liens, claims, interests and encumbrances, subject to the Debtor’s acceptance of higher or otherwise better offers in accordance with the Bidding Procedures.

PLEASE TAKE FURTHER NOTICE that by order, dated November 4, 2026 [Docket No. 106] (the “ Bidding Procedures Order ”), the Bankruptcy Court approved certain relief requested in the related motion [Docket No. 15] (the “ Bidding Procedures Motion ”), and certain procedures that govern the Sale (the “ Bidding Procedures ”). The Bidding Procedures also contain a process for designation of other Additional Stalking Horse Purchasers and related asset purchase agreements for Assets other than the Disney Target Assets, subject to the Debtor’s acceptance of higher or otherwise better offers in accordance with the Bidding Procedures.

Copies of the Bidding Procedures Motion, the Bidding Procedures Order, the Bidding Procedures, and the Stalking Horse Transaction Agreement are available for download at https://cases.stretto.com/chartech (the “ Case Website ”) from the Debtor’s claims and noticing agent, Stretto, Inc. (“ Stretto ”). A separate notice will be provided to counterparties to executory contracts and unexpired leases with the Debtor that may be assumed and assigned in connection with the Sale. Any interested bidder should contact (i) the proposed investment banker to the Debtor, Houlihan Lokey, Attn: Daniel Cullins (dcullins@hl.com); and (ii) proposed counsel to the Debtor, Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati, P.C., Attn: Erin R. Fay (efay@wsgr.com) and Shane M. Reil (sreil@wsgr.com).

• The deadline to submit a bid for any Assets is November 24, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. (ET).

• Any objections to the Sale or the relief requested in connection with the Sale (a “ Sale Objection ”), other than a Contract Objection, which shall be governed by the Assumption and Assignment Procedures, must: (a) be in writing; (b) comply with the Bankruptcy Rules and the Local Rules; (c) set forth the specific basis for the Sale Objection; (d) be filed with the Clerk of the Court, 824 N. Market Street, 3rd Floor, Wilmington, Delaware 19801 on or before November 18, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. (ET) (the “ Sale Objection Deadline ”), and proof of service of such Sale Objection upon the Objection Notice Parties shall be filed with the Court as and when required by the Local Rules; and (e) be served upon the Objection Notice Parties. The “ Objection Notice Parties ” are as follows: (a) proposed counsel to the Debtor, Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati, P.C., 222 Delaware Avenue, Suite 800, Wilmington, Delaware 19801 (Attn: Erin R. Fay (efay@wsgr.com) and Shane M. Reil (sreil@wsgr.com)); (b) proposed investment banker for the Debtor, Houlihan Lokey, (Attn: Daniel Cullins (email: dcullins@hl.com)); (c) counsel to Disney, Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP, One Manhattan West, New York, New York 10001 (Attn: Brandon Van Dyke (brandon.vandyke@skadden.com), Ron E. Meisler (ron.meisler@skadden.com), Bryan Uelk (bryan.uelk@skadden.com), and Samuel J. Cammer (samuel.cammer@skadden.com)); (d) counsel to any official committee of unsecured creditors appointed in the chapter 11 case; and (e) the United States Trustee for the District of Delaware, 844 N. King Street, Suite 2207, Lockbox 35, Wilmington, Delaware, Attn: Linda Casey (Linda.Casey@usdoj.gov).

• An auction for the Assets, unless cancelled or adjourned in accordance with the Bidding Procedures Order, will be held on December 1, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. (ET) , at a location to be determined by the Debtor, or virtually via videoconference pursuant to information to be timely provided by the Debtor to the Auction Participants. As soon as practicable following the conclusion of the Auction, the Debtor will file a notice identifying the Winning Bidder(s).

• Following service of a notice of Auction results, parties may raise objections solely with respect to the conduct of the Auction, the Winning Bidder (only if not a Stalking Horse Purchaser), modifications to any Stalking Horse Agreement, and adequate assurance of future performance by a Winning B
